heard: Persistent myths claim Earth blocks the Sun to change the Moon's shape. This cycle has been tracked for nearly 10,000 years at the Warren Field site in Scotland. The ancient pit alignment beats any other formal record of human timekeeping ever discovered. Despite these millennia of observation, many people still misunderstand the physical trick behind these phases. The Sun constantly illuminates half the Moon, but our viewpoint shifts as it orbits Earth every 27.3 days. We aren't seeing Earth's shadow. We are watching the boundary between lunar day and night from different angles. Outside of rare eclipses occurring twice a year, Earth's shadow never actually touches the moon. The visual illusion remains convincing to this day.
